AI for PDEs in Computational Mechanics

Physics-driven, data-driven, and hybrid approaches: a review of AI4PDEs algorithms, theory, and applications to forward and inverse problems in solid mechanics.

About the speaker

01 / THE TALK

About the talk

Computational mechanics · AI4PDEs · AI4Science · Solid mechanics

Deep learning has spread across many fields, with the combination of artificial intelligence and traditional science (AI for Science, AI4Science) attracting particular attention. Within AI4Science, using AI algorithms to solve partial differential equations (AI4PDEs) has become a focus of computational mechanics. AI4PDEs combines data with equations and can address almost any PDE problem. By incorporating data, its computational efficiency can typically improve by tens of thousands of times compared with traditional algorithms. This talk reviews AI4PDEs research, summarizes existing algorithms and theory, and discusses forward and inverse problems in solid mechanics, before looking ahead to future directions, particularly foundation models for computational mechanics. Existing approaches include physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), deep energy methods (DEM), operator learning, and physics-informed neural operators (PINO). Although AI4PDEs has many scientific computing applications, this talk focuses on solid mechanics. Forward problems include linear elasticity, elastoplasticity, hyperelasticity, and fracture mechanics. Inverse problems include identifying material parameters, constitutive relations, and defects, as well as topology optimization. AI4PDEs offers a new approach to scientific simulation: using large amounts of data to provide approximate solutions for specific problems, then fine-tuning them to the governing physical equations instead of computing from scratch. In this sense, AI4PDEs is a precursor to foundation models for computational mechanics and can substantially accelerate traditional numerical algorithms. AI-assisted scientific computing is an important future direction for both computing and computational mechanics: intelligent computational mechanics.

Speaker’s research & projects

02 / THE SPEAKER

About the speaker

Yizheng Wang

Department of Engineering Mechanics, School of Aerospace Engineering, Tsinghua University

PhD Student

Yizheng Wang is a PhD student in Engineering Mechanics and a Future Scholar at Tsinghua University. His research connects artificial intelligence with physics-based computation (Physical AI), focusing on AI for PDEs and computational solid mechanics. He has worked as a Research Assistant with Microsoft Research AI for Science and visited Bauhaus-Universität Weimar in Germany. His work covers physics-informed neural networks, operator learning, and deep energy methods, with publications in Applied Mechanics Reviews, Nature Communications, JMPS, and CMAME. He has also contributed to an English-language monograph on scientific machine learning.

INVITER / HOST

Bin Cao

Research Scientist

Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab, London

Bin Cao is a Research Scientist at Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab in London, collaborating with Professor Jun Wang at University College London on agents and machine learning for materials science. His research spans scientific agents, crystal representation learning, and Bayesian optimization, combining physical evidence, scientific tools, and research experience to advance materials analysis and discovery. He leads the development of Ganjiang, a self-learning scientific agent exploring intelligent methods for diffraction analysis, phase identification, and structure refinement.
